en.name: Francis Xavier
en.summary: Co-founder of the Jesuits whose missionary voyages brought Christianity to India, Southeast Asia, and Japan.
en.body: Francis Xavier was a Navarrese nobleman who studied alongside Ignatius of Loyola in Paris and became one of the founding members of the Society of Jesus in 1534. Sent east by the Portuguese crown, he spent the following decade preaching across the coasts of India, Sri Lanka, the Malay Peninsula, the Moluccas, and Japan, reportedly baptizing tens of thousands of converts and establishing missions that would shape Catholicism in Asia for centuries. He died in 1552 on an island off the coast of China while attempting to gain entry to the mainland. His incorrupt body is enshrined in Goa, India, where it remains an object of major pilgrimage, and he is regarded as one of the greatest missionaries in Church history.
